text:
```yaml
name: Checks

on:
  push:
    branches: [ main ]
  pull_request:
    branches: [ main ]

jobs:
  build:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest

    strategy:
      matrix:
        node-version: [22]
        pnpm-version: [9]

    steps:
    - name: Checkout code
      uses: actions/checkout@v3

    - name: Set up Node.js ${{ matrix.node-version }}
      uses: actions/setup-node@v3
      with:
        node-version: ${{ matrix.node-version }}

    - name: Install pnpm
      run: npm install -g pnpm@${{ matrix.pnpm-version }}

    - name: Install dependencies
      run: pnpm install --shamefully-hoist --include-dev-dependencies

    - name: Trim devDependencies from pnpm-lock.yaml
      run: |
        pnpm store prune
        pnpm install --shamefully-hoist --filter . --no-lockfile
        pnpm install --shamefully-hoist --filter . --lockfile-only

    - name: Check pnpm-lock.yaml
      run: cat pnpm-lock.yaml
```
This GitHub Actions workflow sets up a job to run on both pushes and pull requests to the main branch. It uses a matrix strategy to test with Node.js version 22 and pnpm version 9. The workflow checks out the code, sets up the specified Node.js version, installs pnpm, and then installs dependencies with the `--shamefully-hoist` and `--include-dev-dependencies` flags. After that, it trims the devDependencies from the `pnpm-lock.yaml` file using the `pnpm store prune` and `pnpm install` commands. Finally, it prints the contents of the `pnpm-lock.yaml` file to verify the changes.
